subject: platform/counter
professional: a web-analytics / privacy engineer who has built cookieless first-party counters (Plausible/GoatCounter style) and reviews them for GDPR/ePrivacy exposure

evidence.correctness: Ran `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in platform/counter: 40 pass, 0 fail. Recomputed independently with a scratch script against core.mjs (inputs I chose, expected values from the stated rules): (1) POST /hit {p:'hub',r:'npm',s:'google'} -> count true, slug hub, ref npm, src google, as README says; slug 'a/../b' and 'Hub' -> rejected 'slug', DNT:1 -> 'opted-out'; (2) sourceOf: www.google.co.uk and news.google.com -> google, evilgoogle.com -> other, t.co -> x, 'constructor' -> other (prototype-key safe via hasOwnProperty); (3) Tally cap 3: adds return true,true,true,false and stored count is 3; (4) deviceClass: Android Mobile -> mobile, Android without Mobile -> tablet, iPad -> tablet; botClass GPTBot -> gptbot, ordinary Chrome -> ''. All matched. Quirk: google.evil.com reads as 'google' (documented label rule; client-side classification so spoofing only inflates the self-reported src: tally). A UA containing 'preview' or 'monitor' is treated as a crawler (BOT_RE substring match), a small false-negative risk for real browsers.
evidence.completeness: README claims checked: POST /hit and GET /counts and /healthz in counter.mjs (present, tested); DNT/Sec-GPC refusal (works); crawler refusal (works); slug regex and 256-byte body cap (works); per-slug-per-day cap (works); ref:/src: breakdowns (works); pull.mjs merge keeping larger count per slug/day (works, tested); site.json off-switch (present, now points at the deployed Worker); usage-data.mjs sync (present, tested); deploy/ Dockerfile, compose, Caddyfile (present, deploy.test.mjs checks them). The Node server does not write geo:/dev:/bot: keys, which only the Worker in platform/edge does; README says the Node server is the not-deployed alternative. Not run end to end here: a live deploy and the daily pull workflow (needs network and credentials).
evidence.verification: Test command `node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 40 pass. Seeded three mutations in core.mjs/pull.mjs and reverted each with git checkout (git status clean): (a) dropped the Sec-GPC check from classify -> 1 test failed (caught); (b) changed the cap comparison `>=` to `>` in Tally.add (off-by-one) -> 1 failed (caught); (c) pull.mjs mergeDays Math.max -> Math.min -> 2 failed (caught). Tests cover the privacy refusals, the cap and the merge rule, so a regression in the core promises is caught. Not covered by a real-socket end-to-end run of the CLI entry point.
evidence.craft: Read core.mjs, counter.mjs, pull.mjs, usage-data.mjs (first 60 lines), site.json. Pure logic split from the Node server so the same rules run in the Cloudflare Worker, no dependencies, atomic store write via tmp + rename, 204 for every refusal so a prober learns nothing, SLUG_RE plus '..' check. Defects: loadStore rethrows on corrupt JSON, so one bad counts.json stops the self-hosted server at start (arguably right, but undocumented); the server flushes only every 60 s and on SIGINT/SIGTERM, so a crash loses up to a minute; the req 'data' handler keeps reading after the body is too big (it drops it but does not destroy the socket); BOT_RE is a broad substring match. No dead code found.
evidence.claims: README claims 'about 200 lines of Node': core.mjs + counter.mjs are 308 lines and the folder is 1,841 lines with tests and pullers, so the figure is stale. README and counter.mjs header frame the counter as serving 'the GitHub Pages catalogue' with 'live_url_visitors: null since the site went up', but CLAUDE.md says the catalogue moved to Cloudflare (marisstella.app) and the live path is the Worker; the README mentions the Worker but keeps the Pages-era framing and the Pages origin in its examples. Backed claims: 'stores one integer per UTC day per slug and nothing else' (Tally shape, tests), 'closed list' of REFS and SOURCES (core.mjs, drift test in attribution), 'unit: not people' (carried in the /counts JSON and pull.mjs output). Deploy instructions use a placeholder domain and were not run. No disclaimer is needed (no user-facing calculator output).
evidence.fitness: Job walked through: an owner wanting cookieless page-load counts committed to the repo. POST /hit -> Tally -> GET /counts -> pull.mjs merge -> summarise (page_loads, top, channels, sources, devices, bots), all exercised by tests and my scratch script; usage-data sync brings the daily branch copy into portfolio/usage. Page totals correctly exclude every prefix: breakdown key. Gap: no unique-visitor measure by design, and the Node server omits the Worker's extra breakdowns.
evidence.domain: Compared against Plausible/GoatCounter practice and ePrivacy/GDPR expectations for cookieless counting: no cookie, no IP stored, no UA stored, closed vocabularies for free-text-derived fields, DNT and GPC honoured server-side and client-side, bots separated, counts labelled as page loads not people. That matches the privacy posture of those tools. Departures: no unique-visitor or session estimate (a deliberate choice), no rate limiting per client (only a per-slug daily cap, which silently stops counting at 20000 and so under-counts a genuinely viral page), and the per-day cap applies to ref:/src: keys too.

defects.what: Per-slug daily cap of 20000 silently stops counting (add returns false, response is still 204): a genuinely viral page is under-counted with no log or flag in the stored data, which contradicts the 'visibly absurd number' rationale for a cap-hit that looks like a plausible figure
README and counter.mjs header say 'about 200 lines' (actual 308 for core+server, 1841 for the folder) and frame the counter around GitHub Pages although the live site is on Cloudflare
BOT_RE substring match ('preview', 'monitor') can classify an ordinary browser UA as a crawler and drop its page load; sourceOf lets google.evil.com read as google
Oversized request bodies are dropped but the socket is still read to completion, and a corrupt counts.json aborts server start without a documented recovery

verdict: A small, honest, well-tested cookieless counter whose core promises (what is stored, what is refused, page totals separate from breakdowns) held up when recomputed with my own inputs: 40 of 40 tests pass and all three seeded mutations (drop Sec-GPC, cap off-by-one, merge max to min) were caught. Privacy design matches what a web-analytics practitioner would expect. It falls to 2 on claims because the README's size figure and Pages-era framing are stale relative to the Cloudflare Worker that is actually live, and the silent cap under-counts a viral page. Meets the bar on the computed rule except claims below 3, so it does not meet the bar; it is finished (completeness 3).
